alternate_names: Sri Lakshmiramana Swamy Temple, Mysuru Palace

history.summary: Consecrated in 1499 during Chamaraja Wodeyar II (Banni mantapa inscription), the oldest of the Amba Vilas Palace temple group; an alternate account credits Vijayanagara king Tuluva Narasa Nayaka. The coronation of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III was held here on 30 June 1799; Narasaraja Wodeyar I added the mantapa and Krishnaraja Wodeyar III built the tower over the mahadwara in 1851. Palace legend holds that Kantirava Narasaraja Wodeyar drank poisoned thirtha here unharmed through devotion, and built the tall gopura in gratitude. ASI-protected monument; coronation history makes it the ceremonially most important of the palace temples.

name: Lakshmiramana Swamy Temple
town_description: Mysuru (Mysore) in southern Karnataka was the royal capital of the Wodeyar dynasty and is famous for the Amba Vilas Palace, Chamundi Hill and its Dasara celebrations.

travel.airport: Mysuru Airport (~12 km); Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~170 km)
travel.railway: Mysuru Junction railway station (~3 km); KSRTC bus station (~2 km)
travel.road: On Ramavilas/Agrahara roads near Mysore Palace; combine with a Mysuru Palace visit

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Dasara season is the most vibrant but busiest
